rules.when: The task is design, architecture, or a clarifying question: system shape, API boundaries, tradeoff analysis, product framing, Lavish planning judgment, or questions the captain must answer before work can be locked. Not bulk implementation and not a mechanical edit.
rules.why: Fable owns judgment, design, architecture, and the hard questions; high-effort Claude (Opus) is the only fallback when the Fable window is tight, never a speed-class harness.

rules.when: The task is fan-out work: generate several rough UI, Paper, or Lavish variants for the captain to compare, or apply an already-decided bulk edit across many artifacts or files. Fast and low-ambiguity; not a final taste pass and not an edit whose content is still an open question.
rules.why: Speed class. Cursor (cursor-agent) first; it has no effort flag. Codex next so Claude quota stays on judgment.

rules.when: The task is a chore: docs, CI hygiene, renames, formatting, dependency bumps, a targeted typo or one-file fix, or other low-ambiguity housekeeping.
rules.why: Fastest cheap path. Cursor first; Codex at low effort as the fallback.

rules.when: The task is frontier implementation: a big or ambiguous multi-file feature, a risky refactor, or any implementation where the architecture is decided but real technical ambiguity remains and a strong coder is needed.
rules.why: Codex is the frontier implementer. Opus at high effort is the fallback when Codex is tight; Fable is not a coder.

rules.when: The task is an ordinary ship: a feature slice, bug fix, or refactor with clear acceptance criteria and limited ambiguity.
rules.why: Ordinary ships are speed-class work; Cursor takes them so Codex and Claude quota stay on frontier work, review, and judgment.

rules.when: The task is code review: adversarial review, a no-mistakes review pass, or a second opinion on code another model authored.
rules.why: Prefer a different family than the author. Codex is the standing reviewer; Opus only when Codex is tight. Review is never Fable work.
